LESSON: READING 8.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POETRY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.4: Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you describe the characters in a poem?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify inanimate characters in a given poem
2. describe traits of inanimate characters present in a given poem
3. appreciate the role of inanimate characters in poetry

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 8.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POETRY
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 8.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POETRY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify inanimate characters in a given poem

What this means
In this part you learn to identify inanimate characters in a given poem. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify inanimate characters in a given poem.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify inanimate characters in a given poem. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe traits of inanimate characters present in a given poem

What this means
In this part you learn to describe traits of inanimate characters present in a given poem. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe traits of inanimate characters present in a given poem.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe traits of inanimate characters present in a given poem. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of inanimate characters in poetry

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of inanimate characters in poetry. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of inanimate characters in poetry.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of inanimate characters in poetry. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify inanimate characters in a given poem)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry to a partner. (skill: describe traits of inanimate characters present in a given poem)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of inanimate characters in poetry)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify inanimate characters in a given poem.
3. Practise this skill: describe traits of inanimate characters present in a given poem.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of inanimate characters in poetry.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you describe the characters in a poem?
2. Why are the characters in a poem important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify inanimate characters in a given poem.
5. Be able to: describe traits of inanimate characters present in a given poem.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
